title: A Line
text: Still Water, an homage to the 2007 exhibition on water. It begins outside: ten metres of water, one hand wide, cut into the paving and pointing at the door.

title: One Drop
text: Inside, a single drop hangs on a hairline. Every four and a half seconds it lets go. The rings reach the rim of the basin just before the next one falls.

title: Falling
text: Seven drops let go from the roof and fall the full height of the building, 8.6 metres, into a basin in the basement. About 1.3 seconds each. Look up, then down.

title: Rain, Indoors
text: Gallery 1 holds nine shallow basins and one private weather. Drops land at random, so no two patterns of rings are ever the same.

title: Still
text: Gallery 2 is given to one long plane of water, a few millimetres deep. Stand at its end: the ceiling, the lights and the columns lie down in it. Every so often, one ring crosses.

title: The Sky, Lowered
text: The sunken court is flooded with a thin sheet of water, so the sky arrives at your feet. Ando's court was always about the sky; here you can look down to see it.
